date: 16th century (de Slane's dating of the manuscript); undated
title: Recipes with the operative words in a numeral-and-letter cipher, two leaves in an Arabic miscellany (BnF Arabe 2562, ff. 54-55)
place: unknown (Egypt likely: the volume opens with a Coptic-year calendar and Nile tables)
shelfmark: Paris, BnF, Département des Manuscrits, Arabe 2562, ff. 54r-55v
folio_note: Four pages (Gallica views 56-58; f. 54r is the left page of view 56, f. 54v-55r are view 57, f. 55v is the right page of view 58), 19-20 lines a page. Each recipe opens with a clear rubric (sifa ..., 'it is good for ...') and clear running words; the names and quantities are in strings of Arabic-Indic numerals (0, 1, 2, 5, 7, 8 most often) mixed with a few detached letters and signs. Roughly half of each page is cipher. Show-through from the other side of the leaf is heavy on the microfilm.
status: De Slane, no. 2562, 3°: 'Feuillet qui paraît avoir appartenu à un recueil de recettes médicales. La plus grande partie du texte est écrite en chiffres et en caractères de convention.' Vajda's index files ff. 54-55 under al-Tibb. Seen on the Gallica microfilm scan 15 Nov 2026: bare cipher inside clear recipe text, no gloss, no key on the leaves. Not on DECODE. No reading found.
why: A sizeable private Arabic cipher of the 16th century with clear context around every cipher string: the hidden words are drug names, quantities and the object of each operation (one recipe speaks of the sages of India and of commanding spirits), so it shows what a practitioner thought worth hiding.

status: Savage-Smith, A New Catalogue of Arabic Manuscripts in the Bodleian Library, I: Medicine (2011), as given in the Fihrist record: 'On folio 101a, between two sections of text, there are some curious letter forms and undeciphered writing.'
